steps.note: S1.3.1.1.1 states rows 0-1 subtract Ja+Rc, rows 2-5 add R(c+Gx)+J(a+Vx), rows 6-7 restore the scratch vectors, so the net target change is (JV+RG)x whatever a,c, as in the paper.
S1.3.1.1.2 gives the bit-network central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, side injection cancelling exactly the intersection-one neighbors, and self coefficient 1.
Same step gives the complex-network central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2 with side injection cancelling intersections zero and two, and self coefficient 1.
S1.3.1.1.3 states X<-X-Y from the inverse schedule, the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x), each invocation restoring its own scratch wires.

The plan only asserts that every edge joins nested nondegenerate labels (S1.3.1.3) and gives two residuals (center P(x)F of dimension h, side 2->5); the per-edge residual table with its dimensions (e.g. B(x)t_X^perp of (a-1)(h-1), side 0->2, scratch last->sink) is never stated.

S1.3.1.3.4 states the side edge 2->5 is nested because <t_X> is inside t_Y^perp for neighbors, with residual P(x)<t_X,t_Y>^perp of dimension h-2; S1.3.1.3.1 supplies the orthogonality of neighboring triple lines.
Only center 3->4 decreases (S1.3.1.3.5), losing h (S1.3.1.3.3); S1.3.1.4 telescopes to sink total Wm-N minus source total N = Wm-2N; S1.3.1.5 adds 2L for the Ic decreasing edges.

S1.3.3.3 only asserts that every nonzero binary residual has an orthonormal basis; the plan never states nondegeneracy plus nonalternation of residuals or the absorption of alternating planes (the w+a, w+b, w+a+b argument).
S1.3.1.6 states L/N is 100/539 for the bit network and 101/539 for the complex network, via L/N=300c/v with c=100 or 101, both below 1/2.
S1.3.3.1 gives the weight identity, additivity mod 4 for orthogonal vectors, and q_V-q_U = sum over an orthonormal basis of wt(v)[v.x] mod 4, negated on a decreasing edge.
S1.3.3.2 states wt(v) is odd, the factor i^{eps[v.x]} = (1+i^eps)/2 + (1-i^eps)/2 (-1)^{v.x}, and H diag(1,-1) H = X turning it into aI+bX_v or its inverse.

The plan counts one kernel per residual vector (S1.3.3, S1.3.3.3) and mentions 'any number of columns' only in the proposition's conclusion; it never states that on k columns the frame change is the product of K_{e,v}^{(x)k}, one tensored factor per residual vector.

S1.3.3.4 gives frames I and C^{(x)m} for zero and full labels, C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a) for X_a->Y_a, repair by Z_{a,k} before and i^{27k}Z_{a,k} after using C=iZC^{-1}Z; S1.3.3.5 negates the physical X outputs.
L/N below 1/2 (S1.3.1.6), deficit N-2L_b>0 and s_b<W_b m (S1.3.2.3), and deficit 2N-2L_c>0 below W_c m (S1.3.3.3) are all stated.
S1.3.4 states both deficits exceed 20*2^-50, log m<20 gives m^{1-2^-50} > m(1-eta), hence s_b/W_b<m^tau and s_c/W_c<m^sigma with tau=sigma=1-2^-50.

S1.4.1.1 states A=E1 Pi E2 with lower-triangular E1,E2 by repeatedly eliminating around the rightmost nonzero entry of the topmost nonzero row, and that Pi has exactly a ones; the clearing operations are only implicit, so this is thin but carries the pivot rule and conclusion.

S1.4.1 only names 'a fixed odd prime q avoiding the denominators of its factorization'; the plan never states the finite table of factors/diagonal numerators or that the rational identities then specialize to Z/q^b with the triangular factors still invertible.

S1.4.1.2 states a lower-triangular change of H or D costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order, each new value a unit multiple plus earlier coordinates still holding original values.
S1.4.1.3 gives D_j<-D_j+H_i, interchange of H_i and D_j, D_j<-H_i-D_j yielding (h+d,d) with one interchange, so a ones cost a interchanges.
S1.5.9 mentions only Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) and C_1 in passing; the definitions E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, nu=min{j: m^j>=B}, C_1=max{20,nu+3}, C_0=128 m B^2 (nu=11, C_1=20) are never given.

The plan's only recurrences are the time recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+... (S1.5.7) and the call-count one; the arithmetic-depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, A(e)<=8e at a leaf and the per-invocation count below E never appear.
S1.5.9 asserts depth at most C_0 d^{C_1} as a result; the unrolling B^{k+1}<=B^2 d^nu and A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1} are not stated.

S1.5.9 states reserving p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits and Delta=o(p) as eps*C_1<1, but not the depth-l induction (values in 2^{-(p+l)}Z[i] of modulus at most 2^l) that makes the reservation exact, so it asserts the conclusion without that sub-derivation.
S1.5.10 states each row of the layer has absolute row sum one, so disk arrays map to disk arrays and the single final truncation errs by less than sqrt2 * 2^-p.

summary: 18 of 26 present, 8 absent, 0 wrong. The plan carries the bank-exchange network (B1-B4), the side-edge, telescoping and loss ratios of the label budget (L2, L3, L5), the phase-interface weight and endpoint steps (P1, P2, P4), all four rank-saving numerics (R1-R4), the matrix-shear elimination, triangular cost and one-interchange steps (M1, M3, M4) and the row-sum truncation bound (S5). It omits the residual table (L1), the nonalternating/orthonormal-basis argument (L4), the k-column tensoring of kernels (P3), the choice of prime and specialization mod q^b (M2), and the whole guard-width derivation (S1-S4), where it only asserts the conclusion Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1})=o(p) and the bit reservation.
